title: The Hobbit
synopsis: Bag End. A round door. Thirteen dwarves on your doorstep singing about gold. There and back again, the wizard says, like that's a small thing.

nodes.text: A cake of plenty. Doors knocking. Maps unrolled.

choices.consequence: “Sign the contract” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Path.
You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Quiet.

nodes.text: Ponies. Songs. Rain.

choices.consequence: The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Joy—follows you into whatever comes next.
The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Honest.

choices.consequence: The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Cunning.

nodes.text: Elves. Sweet bread. Elrond reads the map.

nodes.text: The auction is canceled. Your spoons are mostly accounted for.

choices.consequence: You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Quiet.
The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Spirit.
Some endings reveal themselves last.

nodes.text: You stay home. You write down the journey. Years later your nephew Frodo, reading the book, asks if it's all true. You say, mostly.
You become, in Hobbiton, a quiet author. Children come and ask about the ring. You smile and change the subject.
You keep the ring in your waistcoat. You don't, for many years, look at it. You forget, mostly. It does not, you'll learn later, forget you.
